order: .harness/project.yaml wins over roundtable.yaml, which wins over the defaults

settings.description: The command that checks the app (e.g. python -m pytest tests -q). A task that makes a test fail that passed before is sent back.
Settings for that command, such as QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen. Never keys or passwords.
A command run once before the first task, e.g. pip install -e .[dev].
How many seconds the test or setup command may take.
Where Roundtable's work goes in an existing app. Ending in / means that start plus a name from the goal; anything else is the exact branch. Never main or master.
The files that hold the app's own rules, which every model follows. For a devlog or handoff only the newest entry is read.
At most this many characters of those rules go to the models (headings are always kept).
Only these AI providers may see this project (e.g. deepseek). Empty: any. A role whose models are all from other providers stops the run with a message.
Which set of models builds it (e.g. Budget, Balanced, Quality). Empty: the app's own choice.
Money and effort limits for this project only: max_real_usd_per_run, max_cost_usd, max_attempts_per_task, max_steps_per_task.
Offer looks to choose from before building. auto: only for new apps with screens, or a web app.
Take pictures of the app's screens after each task. auto: when it has screens Roundtable can open.
Before a builder runs a command: off (run it), risky (ask only for risky ones) or all (ask every time). Empty: this computer's choice.
Let the builders look things up on the web (their search words go to a search service). Empty: this computer's choice; a project kept to some providers gets none unless this says on.
Anything the planner should know about this project, in your own words.
